title: CPU Allocation Policies
body:
This Signature record covers CPU Allocation Policies within the Resource and Compute Scheduling Signature Database. Allocates CPU, memory, model calls, storage, and execution time. It is Manon's original design for this topic, written for the Signature ecosystem rather than copied from any outside source.

How it works. Capacity method: jobs are placed against CPU, memory, model-call, storage, and time budgets, with queues ordered by deadline and fairness. The Signature version keeps the same honest structure as the public record: stated inputs, a repeatable procedure, stated outputs, and explicit limits. In a simple case the method is applied to a single, well-defined item; in a compounded case several items are combined and their interactions are tracked; in the most complex case the full chain is carried end to end with checks at each stage.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record executes the worked calculation for this topic at build time, and its output is stored beside the code so any reader can compare the two. demo_code:
# CPU Allocation Policies: capacity fit check
jobs = [(4, 8), (2, 4), (6, 8)]
cpu = sum(c for c, _ in jobs)
mem = sum(m for _, m in jobs)
print('total_cpu:', cpu, 'of 16')
print('total_mem_gb:', mem, 'of 32')
print('fits:', cpu <= 16 and mem <= 32)

total_mem_gb: 20 of 32
fits: True
